observed_title: A sharp Bernstein–type inequality and application to the Carleson embedding theorem with matrix weights
version: Observed arXiv:2110.10730v1, 20 October 2021 watermark; source title page dated October 22, 2021; five PDF pages.

read_ranges.scope: All five PDF pages, both polynomial proofs, matrix application and complete references.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma 1.1: sharp positive polynomial Bernstein bound
assumptions: Positive integer n; p is a complex polynomial, p(s)≥0 for all real s≥0.
|p(s)|≤s^(−1)(1+s)^n for every real s>0. This forces degree p≤n−1.
theorem_cards.statement: |p(0)|≤n². It is sharp, attained by p_n(s)=(1/2)(1+s)^n[1−T_n((1−s)/(1+s))]/s with the removable value at s=0, where T_n is the Chebyshev polynomial.
proof_steps: Set q(z)=zp(z), then deg(q)≤n, q(0)=0, p(0)=q′(0). The Laurent polynomial f(z)=(1+z)^(2n)/(4z)^n q(−((1−z)/(1+z))²) is nonnegative and ≤1 on |z|=1.
By cited Fejér–Riesz factorization f(z)=P(z) overline(P(1/overline(z))) with deg(P)≤n, P zero-free in |z|<1 and |P|≤1 on the circle. Since P(1)=0, |p(0)|=2|f″(1)|=4|P′(1)|².
Cited Lax inequality max|P′|≤n/2 yields n²; P_n(z)=(z^n−1)/2 supplies the witness. Original PDF p3 bars in the reflected conjugate were visually checked; OCR alone loses them.
gaps: Fejér–Riesz factorization and the sharp Lax derivative inequality are external dependencies, not independently proved by this five-page source.

theorem_cards.label: Remark 1: bound without positivity
assumptions: Positive integer n; complex polynomial p with |p(s)|≤s^(−1)(1+s)^n for every s>0; p need not be nonnegative on positive axis.
theorem_cards.statement: The source obtains |p(0)|≤2n²−n and states it is presumably not best possible.
proof_steps: The reduction to g zero-free in the disk is referred to [1]. Lax bounds ||g′||≤n. Cited Rahman–Schmeisser Cor14.2.8 applied to g′ at z=1 yields 2|g″(1)|≤n(2n−1).
gaps: The zero-free reduction and strengthened Bernstein inequality are external dependencies. No claim of sharpness is made.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem A and the claimed 4d² matrix application: literal norm gap
assumptions: W is a d×d matrix-valued measure; A_I positive semidefinite matrices for dyadic intervals I∈D; source refers terminology to Culiuc–Treil [1].
(ii), as printed in this v1 PDF p2, uses Σ_I ||A_I^(1/2)〈Wf〉_I||²|I|≤A||f||²_L², with no W in the RHS norm.
(iii) uses |I_0|^(−1)Σ_{I⊆I_0}〈W〉_I A_I〈W〉_I |I|≤B〈W〉_{I_0} for every dyadic I_0. A and B denote the best embedding and testing constants, not individual matrices.
theorem_cards.statement: The source states equivalence and B≤A≤C(d)B, then improves old C(d)=4e²d² to 4d² via positive-polynomial Lemma1.1 with n=2d. In this local v1 PDF, clause(ii) prints the unweighted L² norm. The literal clause is inconsistent with the claimed equivalent bound, as the scalar check shows. Inferring that the authors intended L²(W) is a reader inference from the cited CT theorem, not an enumerated publisher correction. The official cited Culiuc–Treil Theorem1.2(ii) uses L²(W), with ||f||²_{L²(W)}=∫〈W(dx)f,f〉. Patch/caveat clause(ii) to that weighted norm; retain (i)/(iii) and the matrix method. Under the literal unweighted printing, scalar W=w on [0,1], A_root=1, others0 gives B=w, best (i) A=w, but (ii) A=w²; w=10 yields100>4B40.
proof_steps: Application says only nonnegative polynomials of parameter n=2d are required in [1]; it does not reproduce the matrix embedding proof or define all measure/function notation.

Counterexample binds the exact printed unweighted norm interpretation and v1 page2, visually reread. It restricts that printed clause; it does not invalidate (i)/(iii), the polynomial lemma, or a correctly defined weighted matrix theorem.
gaps: Literal printed clause(ii) remains excluded. The missing-weight interpretation is a reader inference; this card supplies an explicit editorial caveat rather than claiming an official corrected KMR theorem. A weighted 4d² transfer still requires the original CT/KMR hypotheses and external proof dependencies; private HS/cube transfer not certified.
The best embedding constant A and individual matrices A_I are distinct. The CT arXivv2 original open PDF is now downloaded locally and fully read; its separate evidence card is being prepared.

transfer_boundary: The Bernstein polynomial result is adjacent to H05, not a Chernoff mgf bound. Its matrix Carleson application is I04-related with dimension factor 4d², contingent on the original definition and weighted norm contract. It supplies no private cube transfer.
proof_verification: All printed proofs read; conjugation visually checked. External Fejér–Riesz/Lax/Rahman–Schmeisser and Culiuc–Treil dependencies remain unverified; literal TheoremA(ii) norm gap has an explicit scalar check.
